candidate_improvements: Add 'ajv-formats' to package.json and configure it in the AJV instance to support 'uuid' and other standard formats.
Alternatively, replace 'uuid' format in JSON Schemas with a regex pattern to reduce external dependencies.
Upgrade supertest and superagent to their latest major versions to address deprecation warnings and potential security vulnerabilities.
Implement a pre-commit or pre-test hook to validate JSON Schema compatibility with the chosen AJV configuration before running the full test suite.
final_audit_rationale: The application is currently non-functional due to a critical startup error caused by unsupported JSON Schema format in AJV. No core product features (inspection workflow, legal corpus, reports, UI) are implemented or testable. The Definition of Done requires a working, testable application with documented build/run processes, which is not yet achieved. Therefore, a final audit is premature and not recommended.
knowledge_to_carry_forward: AJV (Another JSON Schema Validator) does not support the 'uuid' format by default in recent versions. It requires the 'ajv-formats' package to be installed and explicitly added to the AJV instance.
When defining JSON Schemas for Node.js/Express applications using AJV, always verify format support or use regex patterns for complex identifiers like UUIDs to avoid startup crashes.
The governance infrastructure (autonomy tests, path protection, bootstrap validation) is robust and passed all checks in PDSA-0001.
The basic Node.js/Express project structure and package.json configuration are correct and functional, as evidenced by successful npm install and governance test execution.
Deprecation warnings for supertest/superagent (v6/v8) indicate a need to upgrade to v7/v10+ in future cycles to ensure long-term maintainability and security.
remaining_goal_gaps: DoD-A: The application cannot start due to the AJV schema error, so build/run automation is failing.
DoD-A: Data persistence is not verified as the server crashes before any data operations can occur.
DoD-B: No UI is served, so Arabic RTL interface and user experience requirements are not met.
DoD-C: No inspection workflow endpoints are functional, so the core inspection process cannot be executed.
DoD-D: Legal corpus management and search capabilities are not implemented.
DoD-E: Report generation and analysis features are not implemented.
DoD-F: Security and privacy checks are not fully verifiable as the application is not running.

risks_for_next_cycle: Failure to correctly configure 'ajv-formats' may lead to repeated startup crashes, delaying progress on functional endpoints.
Upgrading supertest/superagent may introduce breaking changes in API usage, requiring test refactoring.
Over-reliance on external libraries for schema validation may increase dependency complexity and maintenance burden.
If the next cycle focuses solely on fixing the schema error without adding functional endpoints, progress toward DoD-A and DoD-B will remain stalled.
